title: Bash failure's 'Command exited with code N' message gets folded behind '… +N lines (ctrl+o to expand)' instead of staying visible
observed: A failing bash call ('echo broke; exit 3') collapses to: 'bash ── auto-approved · 0.0s / Bash echo broke; exit 3 / → broke / (blank) / (blank) / … +1 lines (ctrl+o to expand)' (01-waitfor-timeout-line9.txt) — the diagnostic 'Command exited with code 3' text is never shown; only 'broke' and two blank lines occupy the 3-line collapsed budget.
expected: The most important line on a failed command (the exit-code message) should be visible without expanding, not buried past the collapse cutoff.
design_ref:
internal/tools/bash.go:169-171 (text := outputText + "

" + fmt.Sprintf("Command exited with code %%d", ...) — outputText already ends in its own trailing newline from echo's stdout, so concatenating "

" produces two blank lines before the status text); internal/tui/bridge.go:842,1361 collapsedResultLines=3 caps the committed block at 3 lines total, so 'broke' + 2 blank lines exhausts the budget before the actual status line is reached
